headline: ICE fired seven times into a car. A 5-year-old was in it.
summary: A federal immigration officer shot a 28-year-old Dominican man in the neck in Marble Hill, New York, on Thursday, with a 5-year-old boy in the car. The city's police commissioner says two plainclothes officers approached with a gun drawn as he parked, he pulled forward, and they fired seven rounds. The boy was unharmed. The man lived.

cover_question.q: Why shoot if he was parking?

cover_answer: DHS hasn't said. The city says he pulled forward.
table_question: Should the people enforcing a rule have to show their faces?

5-7.script: Officers who arrest people for the government shot a man in his car in New York yesterday. A boy about kindergarten age was in the car with him. The boy was not hurt and a relative came for him, and the man is alive. The mayor is asking hard questions, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Shielded. If it reaches them: the boy was not hurt, a relative came, the man is alive.
5-7.why_long: Shielded: a six-year-old takes one vivid feature, a boy their own age in that car, for the whole event, so the script settles that first: not hurt, a relative came. No neck, no seven rounds, no masks. The mayor asking questions is the adult on their side. Expect "was the boy scared?" Probably, and he is with his family now.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Two plainclothes federal officers walked up to a car in Marble Hill with a gun out, the commissioner says, as the driver parked. He pulled forward. They fired seven rounds and one hit him below the ear. He lived, the boy with him was not hurt, and the city camera missed the shots: a call with no replay.
8-12.why: The chain in order, and the replay that doesn't exist.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out cause and effect and whether rules were followed, so the script runs the chain in order: the walk-up, the car moving, seven rounds, the camera that missed the shot. The missing replay is the mechanism they know from sport. Expect "who was right?" We don't know yet. Say so.

13-17.script: Why shoot if he was parking? The commissioner says plainclothes officers came up, gun drawn, he pulled forward, they fired seven times. DHS says an officer "discharged his weapon". Second: the mayor says they wore masks. If you can't tell who has the gun, what then?
13-17.why: Two accounts of one minute, then the masks.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two accounts of the same minute, the commissioner's and DHS's, and notice what each leaves out. The mask question asks them to reason from the driver's seat. Expect "was he a criminal?" DHS says a theft conviction and prior arrests. Say that, ask what it licenses, and let them push back.

5-7.a: No. The police said he was not hurt, and a relative came to get him.

8-12.q: Why weren't the officers in uniform?
8-12.a: The mayor says they wore construction vests and masks.

8-12.q: Did the man do something wrong?
8-12.a: DHS says a theft conviction. The city says he was parking.

13-17.q: Why shoot if he was parking?
13-17.a: DHS hasn't said. The city says he pulled forward.

13-17.q: Can the mayor make ICE stop?
13-17.a: No. He pressed Trump and DHS for two hours. Nowhere.
